title: PDF (Apache FOP) and CSV drop-down rendering lists all drop-down options
Description:
Rendering of drop-down field widgets for FOP and CSV screens incorrectly includes all options available for that drop-down rather than the current value for that field.

This behaviour can be observed in the Balance Sheet PDF report from the accounting application. Comparing demo stable to trunk:
 * Stable: [BalanceSheet.pdf (apache.org)|https://demo-stable.ofbiz.apache.org/accounting/control/BalanceSheet.pdf?glFiscalTypeId=ACTUAL&organizationPartyId=Company&thruDate=2024-02-26+01%3A28%3A37.741]
 * Trunk: [BalanceSheet.pdf (apache.org)|https://demo-trunk.ofbiz.apache.org/accounting/control/BalanceSheet.pdf?glFiscalTypeId=ACTUAL&organizationPartyId=Company&thruDate=2024-02-25+22%3A58%3A00.943]

Note: The trunk rendering issue with the _renderSubmitField_ FTL macro is being addressed by OFBIZ-12778.

Proposed fix is to only render the description for a drop-down field's current value for CSV and FO rendering. The relevant macro is _renderDropDownField_ in files:
 * CsvFormMacroLibrary.ftl
 * FoFormMacroLibrary.ftl

title: Move from hard-code menu location to parameterized
Description:
Customization is a key aspect of the OFBiz (Open For Business) platform, providing businesses with a robust and adaptable base to customize their enterprise software solutions according to their unique operational requirements. 

The *Menus.xml file of a component, essential for designing user interfaces that are both intuitive and tailored to the specific roles and tasks of its users, plays a significant role in this context, as referenced within screen widgets and Freemarker templates.

However, as customizations and the project's source code evolve over time, the likelihood of encountering merge conflicts increases significantly, especially when attempting to incorporate customizations alongside ongoing bug fixes and enhancements from the project. 

To improve the appeal of OFbiz and the developer experience, it is recommended to shift from fixed menu locations to a parameterized approach in our components and plugins. This change would enable developers to more seamlessly incorporate a 'custom' menu, facilitating the integration of project updates.

title: Prevent possible file race conditions with SecuredUpload class
Description:
While trying to upload PDF files I found a possible file race conditions in  DataServices::createFileMethod and DataServices::updateFileMethod

The same could exist in several places in ImageManagementServices and ProductServices classes

title: ‎SecuredUpload‎::checkMaxLinesLength put in a regression for PDF files
Description:
As commented at [https://s.apache.org/wpkuj,] while working on OFBIZ-12926 I realised that checkMaxLinesLength put in a possible regression for PDF files.

As a summary: we can't use checkMaxLinesLength for PDF files because they may contain several CharSet encodings. Hence no possibility to use Files::readAllLines that needs a sole CharSet. So we need to bypass this check.

title: Modal title not supported on hyperlink in form fields
Description:
Hyperlinks elements can trigger the opening of a modal window (link-type="layered-modal"). OFBiz uses jQuery UI Dialog to achieve this, and parameters for this library are passed through a set of data-dialog-* ** attributes on the "a" tag, in "HtmlFormMacroLibrary::makeHyperlinkString" Freemarker macro. Then in OfbizUtil.js, links that should open modals are processed : data-dialog-* are used to configure jQueryUI Dialog module.
 
In OfbizUtil.js, data-dialog-text attribute is used to set the title of the modal (text in the colored top bar). The value of this attribute is set using the "text" parameter in  "makeHyperlinkString" macro. However, this macro does not declare a "text" parameter in its signature, and HtmlMacroFormRenderer::makeHyperlinkString does not support it.

 As a result, we cannot set the modal title when using a `hyperlink` tag  with a `text` attribute in a form (although the code indicates otherwise).

This is a subtask for the accounting component. The only changes are to move Groovy tests to main and to accordingly change the references in applications/accounting/testdef/ files.

This fixes the inability to find the files where they are expected. Remains few issues related to the point 3.

title: Issue when caching a query with a selectField
Description:
When a query with a field selection and a cache() option is done, the result is put in cache with the incomplete genericValue (I mean without all the fields).

Then when an other query with the same condition and cache option is done, even whitout the field selection, the result returned is the incomplete version of the GenericValue that has been stored in cache.

The code in the PR prevent from adding in cache an incomplete genericValue and filter the cached value when necessary

title: Use Development Containers as development environments with necessary build tools already available
Description:
Development Containers are becoming a popular method of ensuring a container-based development environment has all the tools needed by a developer to work on a project.

Development Containers ([https://containers.dev/)] depend on the developer's host system running a container runtime, such as Docker. They are supported in IntelliJ and VS Code.

Inclusion of a Development Container configuration in the ofbiz-framework sources will allow new developers to open their IDE with all development tools - such as the correct version of Java SDK - already in place. This should improve the on-boarding experience for new developers.

Outside of IDE integration, tools such as DevPod can be used to create and run Development Containers targeting a project. Users can then SSH into the container and carry out development tasks such as gradle builds. This might be an integration point for IDEs that do not currently have  support Development Containers, such as Eclipse.

[https://blog.jetbrains.com/idea/2024/07/using-dev-containers-in-jetbrains-ides-part-1/]

[https://containers.dev/]

title: String to numeric conversion does not support non-breaking spaces
Description:
When submitting a form with numeric values, OFBiz uses a text input (`<input type="text"/>`), so all characters (entered by hand or pasted) are allowed in the input.

On form's submission, for numeric fields, the string is parsed using `java.text.NumberFormat` class (parse method), using a number instance formatter.

This formatter does not supports non-breaking spaces ('\u00A0', '\u202F', '\u2007'), and characters after a non-breaking space are ignored :

!image-2024-11-05-11-01-13-030.png|width=337,height=153!

This can lead to a situation where a visually correct form stores wrong values :

[^Peek 05-11-2024 10-59.mp4]

One of our client reported this situation while pasting values from external tools. Some values where truncated, because the external tool used non-breaking spaces when displaying values.

You can work around this problem by using an empty string in your properties when you want this boolean to be "false".
A solution would be to use UtilProperties.getPropertyAsBoolean instead.

title: ArithmeticException when producing inventory with general cost set on routing task
Description:
h3. {*}Description{*}:

We are encountering a runtime exception when attempting to produce inventory from a *Production Run* in the *Manufacturing* module. This issue specifically occurs when a *general cost* is configured on a {*}routing task{*}.
----
h3. {*}Steps to Reproduce{*}:
 # Navigate to the *Manufacturing > Production Run* module.

 # Create a Production Run for any finished good item.

 # Assign a routing that includes one or more routing tasks.

 # On any of the routing tasks, set a *general cost* (e.g., other fixed cost).

 # Start the production run and complete the tasks.

 # Try to *produce inventory* using the "Produce" button.

h3. {*}Expected Behavior{*}:

The inventory should be produced successfully, and unit cost should be calculated based on total cost and quantity.
----
h3. {*}Actual Behavior{*}:

The system throws the following exception:
java.lang.ArithmeticException: Non-terminating decimal expansion; no exact representable decimal result.
	at java.base/java.math.BigDecimal.divide(BigDecimal.java:1780)
	at org.apache.ofbiz.manufacturing.jobshopmgt.ProductionRunServices.productionRunProduce(ProductionRunServices.java:1872)
 
This happens when {{unitCost = totalCost.divide(quantity)}} is called and the result is a non-terminating decimal (e.g., 10 / 3).

title: Error when forcing PO completion if receipt contains rejected units
Description:
When a PO receipt contains rejected units, clicking the *“Force Complete Purchase Order”* button in the Order Details screen generates an error because the {{cancelRemainingPurchaseOrderItems}} service does not take rejected items into account when computing the units to cancel.

 

The issue can be reproduced as follows.

 

Create a PO for, e.g., 10 units of WG-1111 and approve it.

In the ‘Actions’ sections of the order details screen, click the ‘Receive’ button.

  !1_Receive_annotated.png|width=467,height=294!

 

Select the automatically created shipment and click ‘Receive Selected Shipment’.

!2_Receive_Selected_Shipment_annotated.png|width=314,height=167!

 

 Receive 8 units of WG-1111, reject 1 and click ‘Receive Selected Product(s)’.

!3_Receive_Selected_product(s)_annotated.png|width=599,height=216!

 

 Go back to the order details screen, e.g., by clicking the PO id in the ‘Receipt(s) For Purchase Order …’ recap section.

!4_Receipt(s)_For_Purchase_Order_annotated.png|width=652,height=224!

 

Click ‘Force Complete Purchase Order’ in  the ‘Actions’ section of the Order details screen.

!5_Force_Complete_Purchase_Order_annotated.png|width=429,height=323!

 

An error is generated because of an invalid cancel quantity computation in the 'cancelRemainingPurchaseOrderItems' service.

!6_Error_cannot_cancel_annotated.png|width=554,height=119!

 

The problem is that, currently, the service only accounts for accepted quantities, 8 in our example, and doesn’t take into account rejected units, 1 in our example. Hence, the service tries to cancel 2 units ( = 10 –  8) from the 10 units ordered, but an error is generated because there is only 1 unit ( = 10 – 8 – 1) available to cancel.

            .makeValidContext('sendMailFromScreen', 'IN', ctx)

title: Remove deprecated and defunct 3rd Party Payment Integrations from applications
Description:
Remove the following payment gateway integrations from {{applications/accounting/}} whose third-party APIs and SDKs are no longer operational, deprecated, and haven't been maintained for a while:
 * PCCharge & RITA (GO Software / Verifone): Verifone announced end-of-life in April 2015; all support terminated on October 1, 2015. Both communicate over raw TCP/IP sockets to a local Windows daemon with no cloud successor.
Ref: [https://3dmerchant.com/blog/merchant-processing-industry-news/pccharge-life-notice-verifone]
 * ClearCommerce: Acquired by FIS. Implemented back in 2006 and never really maintained. The original platform and its test endpoint are no longer reachable.
 * Orbital (Chase Paymentech / Fiserv): Deprecated; no new onboarding available. The proprietary SDK is no longer distributed and the integration is already excluded from standard compilation.
 * Payflow Pro (PayPal): Officially labeled "legacy" by PayPal. ACH closed May 2021, 3DS v1.x  deprecated October 2022. The SDK ({{{}paypal.payflow.PayflowAPI{}}}) is unavailable in any public repository and excluded from compilation.
 * PayPal NVP / Classic API: Officially labeled "legacy". All dependent resources (Orders v1, Payments v1, Billing Agreements, etc.) are formally deprecated by PayPal. The SDK ({{{}com.paypal.sdk.core.nvp.*{}}}{color:#0a0a0a}) is unavailable publicly and excluded from compilation.{color}Ref: [https://developer.paypal.com/api/rest/deprecated-resources/]
Ref: [https://developer.paypal.com/api/nvp-soap/]
 * {color:#000000}WorldPay: The specific product this integration targets, WorldPay Select Junior, is absent from Worldpay's current developer documentation entirely. The integration uses a redirect-based flow ({{{}instId{}}} parameter, {{{}[select.worldpay.com|http://select.worldpay.com/]{}}}) with no equivalent in the current Access Worldpay REST API.{color}
{color:#000000}Ref: [https://developer.worldpay.com|https://developer.worldpay.com/]{color}

 * SecurePay (Australia):{color:#000000} The integration uses the proprietary {{securepay.jxa}} Java SDK targeting {{{}[https://api.securepay.com.au/xmlapi/payment]{}}}, which has no public repository or Maven artifact. SecurePay has been acquired by Fat Zebra, whose platform is built on REST APIs with no equivalent to this XML-based integration. The integration is already excluded from standard compilation in {{build.gradle}} due to the missing SDK.{color}Ref: [https://www.fatzebra.com/blog/fat-zebra-acquires-securepay]

 * eWay (Australia): {color:#000000}The integration targets hardcoded legacy {{.asp}} XML endpoints ({{{}[https://www.eway.com.au/gateway/xmlpayment.asp]{}}}, {{{}gateway_cvn/xmlpayment.asp{}}}) from eWAY's original gateway circa 2003. eWAY has fully replaced this with the Rapid API (REST/JSON). NetSuite has officially retired the eWAY XML gateway integration.{color}Ref: [https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/netsuite/ns-online-help/section_1492528191.html]
Ref: [https://eway.io/api-v3/]

 * {color:#000000}SagePay (now Elavon/Opayo): The integration targets SagePay's VPS Protocol v3.00, communicating with {{*.[sagepay.com|http://sagepay.com/]}} endpoints. SagePay was sold to Elavon in 2020 and rebranded as Opayo. Protocol v3.00 has since been mandated for removal in favour of v4.00, and all legacy {{[sagepay.com|http://sagepay.com/]}} URLs ({{{}[live.sagepay.com|http://live.sagepay.com/]{}}}, {{{}[test.sagepay.com|http://test.sagepay.com/]{}}}) stopped working after March 31, 2024.{color}

 * {color:#000000}CyberSource ICS (Simple Order API / SOAP): The integration uses the {{com.cybersource.ws.client}} SOAP SDK targeting API version 1.43. CyberSource has mandated migration away from the Simple Order API to its REST API, stating that users "must migrate" to REST-based services. Additionally, the SOAP API's current username/password authentication will be rejected after June 24, 2026, with no path to continue using the Simple Order API beyond that point without a full re-implementation. The integration is already excluded from standard compilation in {{build.gradle}} due to the missing SDK JAR.{color}Ref: [https://developer.cybersource.com/docs/cybs/en-us/rb-upgrade/migration/all/na/recurring-billing-upgrade/rb-upgrade-actions/rb-upgrade-updating/rb-upgrade-apis.html]
Ref: [https://developer.cybersource.com/docs/cybs/en-us/so-p12/migration/all/so/so-p12/so-p12-intro.html]

 * {color:#000000}Authorize.Net AIM: The integration posts to {{transact.dll}} using Name-Value Pair (NVP) fields prefixed with {{x_}} — the exact pattern Authorize.net has deprecated. AIM is officially labeled "Deprecated" and will no longer receive updates including payment network mandate compliance updates.{color}Ref: [https://developer.authorize.net/api/upgrade_guide.html]

Dev Mailing List Reference: https://lists.apache.org/thread/tdcgcq63k2m96vrjkl91w9691zvbvog8

title: Remove the WebPOS plugin and move to the attic
Description:
Remove the WebPOS plugin.

[https://github.com/apache/ofbiz-plugins/tree/trunk/webpos]



This proposal is not based on the relevance of POS systems. POS solutions remain an important part of retail operations. However, the current WebPOS implementation appears to be based on an architectural approach that is no longer aligned with modern POS development practices.

Some observations:
 * Modern POS solutions are increasingly built as mobile applications, PWAs, or API-driven frontends.

 * OFBiz already provides backend capabilities such as catalog management, pricing, inventory, order management, and accounting, which can be exposed through APIs.

 * Maintaining a dedicated POS frontend within OFBiz may not provide significant value compared to allowing specialized frontend applications to consume OFBiz services.

 * Modern POS requirements often include offline capabilities, mobile device support, hardware integrations, and rich user experiences that are difficult to achieve within the current WebPOS architecture.

 * There are many mature frontend technologies available today (React, Vue, Flutter, React Native, Ionic, etc.) that can be used to build POS applications on top of OFBiz APIs.

 * The plugin appears to have limited community activity and maintenance compared to other areas of OFBiz.

Instead of continuing to maintain WebPOS, the community could focus on strengthening API capabilities and integration patterns, enabling developers to build modern POS applications using the frontend technology of their choice.

As a first step, we could consider:
 # Evaluating current WebPOS adoption.

 # Identifying active maintainers and users.

 # Deprecating the plugin if community interest is low.

 # Eventually archiving or removing the plugin if no active maintenance exists.

title: The port offset is being applied twice when loading WebSite properties.
Description:
In the method {{{}from(GenericValue){}}}, web site default settings are loaded. Configurations are overridden by the WebSite being used. In particular, a port offset is always added here, which can be set via the start parameters. Therefore, it is not necessary to adjust the WebSite entry in the database to store an alternative port to 8443. The method {{from(HttpServletRequest)}} calls the method {{from(GenericValue)}} itself and additionally sets the port offset. The result is that an offset is added twice.

My suggestion is that {{addPortoffset}} is initialized with {{false}} and only set to {{true}} when new WebSiteProperties are created.

title: Apache OFBiz MRP — Procurement Lead Time Not Applied to Purchase Requirements
Description:
_Feature gap / enhancement request · verified on trunk (commit 18109c9fe7), Java 17, demo data_
h3. Use case

When MRP plans a purchased item, the proposed purchase requirement's start date should fall early enough for the component to arrive by the date it is needed — i.e. the supplier's procurement lead time should offset the requirement start date from its required-by date. This lets planners know when each PO must be placed.
h3. Feature gap

MRP currently does not factor procurement lead time into purchase requirements. Every proposed PRODUCT_REQUIREMENT is created with {*}requirementStartDate = requiredByDate{*}, so the "place the PO by" signal is lost. With any non-zero supplier lead time, a PO created from such a requirement is placed too late and the component arrives late by exactly the lead time.
 * *SupplierProduct.standardLeadTimeDays* is not read by MRP (only by order-entry display screens).
 * *ProductFacility.daysToShip* is honored only for demand originating from the confirmed sales order and is forced to 0 for purchased item demand, so setting it on components has no effect.

h3. Verification (skateboard two-level BOM, 7 purchased leaf components, 15-day supplier lead time)
||Scenario||Purchase requirement dates||Result||
|Baseline (no daysToShip)|start = required-by|No lead-time offset|
|daysToShip = 15 on components|start = required-by|Setting ignored for components|
|daysToShip = 15 on sales-order product|whole tree shifts as one block; start still = required-by|Still no procurement offset|

Manufactured items are correctly back-scheduled through their routings; only purchased requirements lack the procurement offset. Example — Glue needed Jun 1: proposed start Jun 1, expected start ≈ May 17 (Jun 1 − 15 days).
h3. Expected behavior
{code:java}
Requirement Start Date = Required-by date − procurement lead time{code}
The procurement lead time should determine when a purchase requirement must be initiated so the component is available when needed.
h3. Evidence

!06_supplier_leadtime.png!
_Supplier record for Glue — standardLeadTimeDays = 15. This value is configured but does not get factored/honored by MRP._

!tc1_baseline_requirements.png!
_Baseline MRP run — every purchased PRODUCT_REQUIREMENT has requirementStartDate equal to requiredByDate (no procurement offset); only manufactured items are back-scheduled._

!tc3_finishedgood_requirements.png!
_Even with delivery days set, the proposed purchase requirements still have requirementStartDate equal to requiredByDate — the supplier's delivery time is not factored into the dates._

title: MRP applies the global SUPPLIER calendar to resolve ProductFacility.daysToShip instead of Facility specific Calendars
Description:
Currently in MRP, the {{requirementStartDate}} for a purchased product (no BoM) is computed by walking backward from the {{requiredByDate}} over a single global {{TechDataCalendar}} with {{{}calendarId = "SUPPLIER"{}}}.

Part of that backward offset is {{ProductFacility.daysToShip}} (honoured for {{SALES_ORDER_SHIP}} events). However, {{daysToShip}} is a *facility-level* attribute representing handling/ship work performed at the facility — so applying a *supplier-side* calendar doesn't look like a sound approach.

OFBiz already models facility-specific calendars via the {{FacilityCalendar}} entity ({{{}facilityId{}}} -> {{{}calendarId{}}}, with {{{}fromDate{}}}/{{{}thruDate{}}} and a {{facilityCalendarTypeId}} discriminator), mirroring the established {{FixedAsset.calendarId}} pattern. However, {{FacilityCalendar}} and {{FacilityCalendarType}} are currently {*}dormant{*}: there are no references to them in any Java, Groovy, service, or screen definition, and no seed/demo data exists. The current {{{}SUPPLIER{}}}-calendar usage is legacy — the affected code block historically carried a {{// TODO: REVIEW this code}} comment, and {{SUPPLIER}} was the only calendar that path ever consulted.
h2. Proposed change
 # Resolve the {{daysToShip}} working calendar from {{FacilityCalendar}} for the requirement's {{{}facilityId{}}}, using some dedicated {{facilityCalendarTypeId say "SHIPPING"}} (a new seeded type), filtered active by date.
 # Walk {{daysToShip}} backward over that facility calendar.
 # Fall back to the global {{DEFAULT}} calendar, then to direct day arithmetic, when no facility calendar is configured.

Suggested resolution order for {{{}daysToShip{}}}:
{code:none}
FacilityCalendar(facilityId, facilityCalendarTypeId="SHIPPING", active) -> calendarId -> global "DEFAULT" TechDataCalendar -> direct day arithmetic (no calendar)
{code}
h2. Seed data

Add a new facility calendar type (and optionally demo {{FacilityCalendar}} rows):
{code:xml}
<FacilityCalendarType facilityCalendarTypeId="SHIPPING" description="Shipping/handling working calendar"/>
{code}
h2. Backward compatibility
 * Behaviour changes *only* for purchased products at facilities that have a {{SHIPPING}} {{FacilityCalendar}} configured. With none configured, the result is identical to today (global DEFAULT calendar, or direct arithmetic when absent).
 * This activates the previously-unused {{FacilityCalendar}} / {{FacilityCalendarType}} entities for their intended purpose.
 * The pre-existing limitation that {{TechDataServices}} backward functions ({{{}capacityRemainingBackward{}}}, {{{}endPreviousDay{}}}) do not honour {{TechDataCalendarExcDay}} / {{TechDataCalendarExcWeek}} exception days applies equally here and is {*}out of scope{*}.

title: Open combined PDF in browser from Find Orders Print (PDF) action when no printer is selected
Description:
*Current behavior*

On Find Orders (ordermgr), the "Print (PDF)" mass action renders one PDF per selected
order and sends each as a print job to the selected printer. When no printer is
selected, the jobs go silently to the server's default printer and nothing is shown
in the browser.

*Improvement*

When no printer is selected, open one combined PDF containing all selected orders in
a new browser tab instead of printing. When a printer is selected, keep the current
behavior and spool the jobs to that printer.

*Proposed fix*

# Add a request-map \{{orders.pdf}} in the ordermgr controller, backed by a Java event
  that loops the selected orderIdList, renders the existing
  \{{OrderPrintScreens.xml#OrderPDF}} screen per order through the existing
  ScreenRenderer + FOP pipeline, merges the results with PDFBox
  \{{PDFMergerUtility}} (already an OFBiz dependency), and streams the combined PDF
  inline as \{{application/pdf}}.
# In \{{FindOrders.ftl}}, adjust runAction() so that when the selected action is
  massPrintOrders and no printer is selected, the form submits to \{{orders.pdf}} with
  target _blank; otherwise it submits as today.

*Notes*

- Depends on OFBIZ-13505, which fixes the rendering defects currently breaking the
  mass PDF actions.
- Existing printing and Create File behavior is unchanged.

title: Auto-generated indicator (Y/N) fields silently default to "Y" and overwrite a NULL value on unrelated form saves
Description:
*Problem*

{{ModelFormFieldBuilder.induceFieldInfoFromEntityField()}} builds the auto-generated {{<drop-down>}} control for an {{{}indicator{}}}-type entity field differently depending on context:
 * For {{find}} forms, the option list includes a blank option:

 
{quote}^{{List<OptionSource> optionSources = UtilMisc.toList(}}^
^{{new ModelFormField.SingleOption("", null, null),}}^
^{{new ModelFormField.SingleOption("Y", null, null),}}^
^{{new ModelFormField.SingleOption("N", null, null));}}^
{quote}
* For {{{}create{}}}/{{{}update{}}} forms, it does not:

 
{quote}~{{List<OptionSource> optionSources = UtilMisc.toList(}}~

{{~new ModelFormField.SingleOption("Y", null, null),~}}
{{~new ModelFormField.SingleOption("N", null, null));~}}
{quote}
When the underlying column is nullable and its current value is {{NULL}} (no default-value, never set by demo/seed data), the rendered {{<select>}} has no option matching the current value, so the browser falls back to highlighting the first {{<option>}} — "Y". Submitting the form for _any_ reason, including editing a completely unrelated field, then silently persists {{"Y"}} into a column that was previously unset.

*Concrete reproduction*

{{ProductStore.allocateInventory}} is a nullable {{indicator}} field with no default value, left {{NULL}} by demo data. {{EditProductStore}} ({{{}applications/product/widget/catalog/StoreForms.xml{}}}) picks it up via {{<auto-fields-service service-name="updateProductStore"/>}} with no explicit {{<field>}} override. Editing any other Product Store field and saving flips {{allocateInventory}} from {{NULL}} to {{{}Y{}}}, which quietly disables inventory reservation for sales order items unless they carry {{autoReserve=true}} ({{{}OrderServices.reserveInventory(){}}}).

Note: {{allocateInventory}} itself already has a narrower, pre-existing fix (OFBIZ-12001 / PR #1237) that forces the field's _display_ default to "N" via {{no-current-selected-key="N"}} on an explicit {{<field>}} override. That addresses the symptom for this one field (and changes which value gets silently written from Y to N), but does not address the general framework-level gap: any other nullable {{indicator}} field picked up through entity/service auto-fields with no explicit override is equally exposed to a null-to-non-null value being silently written on an unrelated save.

*Proposed Improvement (framework-level)*
 * In {{{}ModelFormFieldBuilder.induceFieldInfoFromEntityField(){}}}, add the blank {{SingleOption}} to the create/update branch as well, gated on {{!modelField.getIsNotNull()}} — so a genuinely {{NOT NULL}} column without an explicit override still gets a forced real default, while nullable columns preserve {{NULL}} when untouched.
 * In {{{}GenericEntity.set(){}}}, normalize a blank string submitted for an {{{}indicator{}}}-typed field to {{null}} before it reaches the datastore, so the blank option round-trips as {{NULL}} rather than being persisted as {{{}""{}}}.
 * Add unit test coverage in {{ModelFormFieldBuilderTest}} for: nullable indicator → blank/Y/N options on update forms; {{NOT NULL}} indicator → Y/N only; find forms → always blank/Y/N (unchanged).

*Discussion*

Raised on [dev@ofbiz.apache.org|mailto:dev@ofbiz.apache.org] ("[DISCUSS] Auto-generated indicator fields silently default to first <option> (Y/N) when unset - framework-level fix?", 2026-08-24). Community feedback (Divesh Dutta) favored the framework-level fix over a per-field patch, since the per-field approach doesn't prevent recurrence for other entities' nullable indicator fields.

*Related:* OFBIZ-12001 (PR #1237) — prior narrower fix for {{ProductStore.allocateInventory}} display default.
